sentences.text: This claim petition is filed under section 166 of the M.V. Act, seeking compensation for the injuries sustained in a road traffic accident.

2. The facts leading to the filing of the instant petition are that on 30.03.2024 at about 2.30 a.m.,
when the petitioner was riding his motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KL-41-R-4810 along with pillion rider on the extreme left side of B.B.Road in slowly and cautiously by observing all the traffic rules and regulations, when he reached near Sanjeeviningar, Kodegehalli Flyover, Bengaluru City, the driver of car bearing Reg.No.KA-51-AA- 7363 which was moving ahead of the motorcycle in a rash and negligent manner, endangering human life, without giving any signal or indicator suddenly applied break, as a consequence of which the motorcycle dashed against car and fell down along with the motorcycle and sustained grievous injuries.

It is further urged that the petitioner was shifted to Manipal Hospital, Bengaluru wherein first aid treatment was provided and then he was shifted to St.John's Hospital, wherein he was treated as inpatient and underwent several examinations and was discharged with an advice to take complete bed rest and regular followup treatment.
He spent substantial amount towards his treatment.
Further at the time of accident she was hale and healthy and he was brilliant student studying Bachelor of Physiotherepy course.
Due to the accident he cannot concentrate on his studies and in future the petitioner cannot participate in any co-curricular activities.
It is further urged that the accident happened because of rash and negligent manner of driving of the aforesaid car by its driver.
The respondent No.1 & 2 being the owner and insurer are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation, as such prayed to grant a compensation amount.
3. Notice was duly served to respondent No.1, the respondent No.1 did not appear before this Tribunal.
Hence he placed exparte.
4. After service of notice, respondent No.2 filed written statement by contending that the petition itself is not maintainable either law or on facts.
This respondent denied the issuance of insurance policy in respect of car bearing Reg.No.KA-51-AA-7363.
However the liability if any is pleaded to be subject to the terms & conditions of the policy.
Further the respondent has contended that, the owner and the concerned police have not complied the mandatory provision of Sections 134(c) and 158(6) of M.V.Act.
This respondent specifically and empathically denied the occurrence, mode and manner of accident and also involvement of the vehicle in the accident.

Further it is contended that the alleged accident was happened due to the self negligence of the rider of the motorcycle and caused this accident, hence there is no negligence on the part of the driver of car.
Further the rider of the motorcycle was driving the vehicle rash and negligent manner and failed to abide traffic rules,
thus , is sole responsible for the accident.
The petitioner himself riding the motorcycle and he being third party being a tortfeasor as such is not entitled to claim compensation in the matter.
The petition is bad for non-joinder of necessary party.

Without prejudice to the said contention it is averred that the driver of the offending car and rider of the motorcycle did not possess valid &
effective DL as on the date of accident.
On account of willful breach of the terms & conditions of the policy by the insured, the insurance company is not liable to indemnify him.
Further denied all the allegation made in the petition.
Hence prayed to dismiss the petition.

5. On the basis of above pleadings the following issues were framed :

sentences.text:
Whether the petitioner proves that he sustained injuries in a road traffic accident that occurred on 30.03.2024 at about 2.30 a.m., near Sanjeeviningar cross, on B.B.
Road, Kodegehalli Flyover towards Airport, Bengaluru City due to actionable negligence of the driver of car bearing Reg.No.KA-51-AA-7363 ?

2) Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation as prayed for ? If so, at what rate and from whom ?
3) What order or award ?
6. The petitioner examined himself as PW.1.
Ex's .P1 to 25, Ex.P.37 & 38 were marked on his behalf.
The MRO of Manipal Hospital was examined as PW.2.
Ex.P.26 to 30 were marked through him.
Further the MRO at St.Johns Hospital was examined as PW.3, through him Ex.P.31 to 34 got marked.
Dr.Nagaraj. B.N, Orthopedic Surgeon was examined as PW.4.
Ex's .P35 & 36 were marked through him.
The respondent No.2 did not choose to lead any evidence on its behalf.
7. Heard counsel for the petitioner and respondent No.2 counsel on merits.
Perused the entire materials placed on record.

8. This tribunal answers to the above issues are as follows :-
Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative Issue No.2 : Partly in the Affirmative Issue No.3 : As per final order for the following :
REASONS 9. ISSUE NO.1: There is no dispute regarding the occurrence of the accident on the relevant date,
time and place.
The injuries sustained by the petitioner in the road traffic accident is also not in conflict.
The only issue with which the parties are at loggerheads is with regard to the factum of negligence.

As manifest from the police records and testimony of PW.1, on an early morning of 30.03.2024 i.e., at 2.30 a.m., the driver of car bearing Reg.No.,KA-51-AA-7363 (which was proceeding ahead of the petitioner's motorcycle) applied the brakes suddenly without giving any indication.

Under such circumstances, it appears in all probability that by the time the rider of motorcycle / petitioner realized the said fact, it would have been too late for him to react and check or divert his vehicle to avoid collision.
What also deserves notice is that the accident occurred on a highway where the vehicles normally are permitted and accordingly ply at a speed of 80 to 120 kmph.
Hence despite putting best efforts the rider of motorcycle / petitioner could not have controlled his vehicle and thereby dashed against the car.

In this view of the matter, no negligence can be imputed on the part of the petitioner and it is amply clear that the resultant accident occurred due to the sole negligence of the driver of car bearing Reg.No.KA-51-AA-7363.

jurisdictional police have also filed charge sheet against him for the offences punishable u/s's 279,
338 of IPC.
There is nothing on record to believe that the charge sheet filed by the police is defective or collusive.
Further Regulation No.24 of the Rules of Road Regulations 1989 prescribes that 'No driver of a vehicle shall apply brake abruptly unless it is necessary to do so for safety reasons'.
In the present case nothing is placed on record to show that there was sufficient reason for the driver of the car to apply sudden brakes.
Even otherwise when the charge sheet is filed against the driver of the car for rash and negligent driving, burden was cast on the owner as well as insurer thereof to disprove the same.
Claimants cannot be called upon to prove a negative factor.
For the best reasons known to him, the owner of the offending car (respondent No.1) failed to appear before this Tribunal despite due service of the notice of petition upon him.
Accordingly an adverse inference could be drawn against him that he has impliedly admitted the petition averments.
10. Though the respondent No.2 Insurance company denied the cause of the accident, it has not let in any cogent evidence to prove its defence.
No independent witness was either produced by the insurer of the car to displace the version of the accident as deposed by PW.1 in this case.
Hence the respondents No.2 utterly failed to discharge the burden that was placed on them.
Added to this the respondent No.2 did not make any attempt to examine the driver of its offending car who is the best witness to depose about the cause of accident.
There is no explanation to that effect.
Non-examination of the said driver is fatal to the defence of respondent No.2.
Hence its contention that there was no negligence on the part of driver of car has to be disbelieved.

Furthermore the fact that the said driver of car suo-moto pleaded guilty in the C.C.1736/2024 case registered against him goes to show that he admitted the negligence on his part that led to occurrence of accident in which the petitioner sustained injuries.
Under such circumstances the evidence of PW.1 which is supported by police documents has to be accepted.
Consequently I hold that the accident is proved to have been caused due to the actionable negligence of the driver of the offending car bearing Reg.No.KA-51-AA-7363 is proved.

With this observation issue No.1 is answered as 'In the Affirmative'.
11. ISSUE NO.2 :
As already discussed above the petitioner has proved that the accident took place due to the actionable negligence of the driver of car.
Therefore he is entitled for compensation.
12. AGE, AVOCATION AND INCOME :

The petitioner has exhibited his Aadhar card at Ex.P12,
wherein his date of birth is reflected as 15.09.2003.
This indicates that he was aged (20 years 6 months 15 days) 21 years on the date of accident.
13. Ex.P.14 make it evident that the petitioner is studying Bachelor of Physiotherapy (BPT) at MVM College of Physiotherapy in third year BPT Course.
That means to say the petitioner was a non-earning person at the time of accident.
However it is relevant to note that he is an Bachelor of Physiotherapy Student who has good career prospects.

14. It is relevant to relying on the decision of the Hon'ble High Court reported in 2020 0 Supreme(Kar) 104 (Shri Mallikarjun S/o. Yallappa Jogannavar and Ors. vs. Shri Umesh M. S/o.
Murthy K. and Ors.) wherein the deceased in the above cited decision was an engineering student and the Hon'ble Court had considered his income at Rs.25,000/- p.m. and granted compensation.

The Bachelor of Physiotherepy cannot be equated with the B.E. or MBBS.
No doubt this tribunal is not trying to draw a distinction between these two degrees or making an attempt to discriminate on the basis of societal mindset.
The Bonafide letter issued by MVM College of Physiotherapy discloses that the petitioner was studying in third year BPT Course.
No doubt his studies might have improved during his degree days.
But the mere fact of petitioner pursuing his BPT Course goes to show that he had bright future.
Therefore, Rs.20,000/- has to be taken into consideration as monthly income of the petitioner.

sentences.text: When such is the case physical disability assessed by the medical expert is on the higher side.
All injuries and assessment of disability do not impact the earning capacity, nor in a similar way.
The disability has to be seen in the context of the particular occupation or calling that the victim is engaged in.

The co-relation between the physical disability suffered in an accident and the loss of earning capacity resulting from it was considered in great detail by the Hon'ble Apex Court in Rajkumar V/s Ajaykumar and another reported in (2011) 1 SCC 343.

entities.text: Rajkumar V/s Ajaykumar and another reported in (2011) 1 SCC 343
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the said case, the Apex Court held that it is the functional disability which would be the operative criteria for assessing the loss of future earnings and not the physical disability.
Therefore compensation for loss of future earning has to be just & proper so as to enable him to live a life of dignity.

19. The point that merits consideration is that as per the ratio laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Rajkumar V/s Ajaykumar, the doctor who treated an injured claimant or who has subsequently assessed his extent of permanent disability can give evidence only in regard to the extent of permanent disability.
The loss of earning capacity is something that will have to be assessed by the Tribunal with reference to the evidence in entirety.

Thus in compliance of the ratio of the Hon'ble Apex Court as stated supra, on appreciating the evidence on record, the loss of earning capacity of the petitioner according to this Tribunal may be as high as 100%, but in no case it would be less than 28%.
Accordingly the compensation for the loss of the petitioner's future earning must be computed on that basis.

22. LOSS OF INCOME DURING LAID-UP PERIOD:
Considering the nature of injuries, treatment given and duration of his stay in the hospital, it is quite natural that petitioner could not have carried out his education for at least 6 months.

Thus by taking into account the notional income of the petitioner,
this Tribunal awards Rs.1,20,000/- (20,000 X 6) under this head.
23. MEDICAL EXPENSES :
As per the bills marked at Ex.P22, the petitioner has spent Rs.10,62,756/- towards medical expenses.
During the course of his cross examination he categorically admitted that he has reimbursed Rs.4,00,000/-.
On perusal of Ex.P.22 of Inpatient bill of Manipal Hospitals, the said bill is xerox copy.
Further on perusal of Specialists Hospital Inpatient bill summary, the said bill is Coloured xerox copy.

Further the inpatient bill of Specialists Hospital,
bill date 30.05.2024, wherein the bill discloses that in the customer column : Health Insurance TPA of India Ltd., Further in the said documents it also written as total bill amount is Rs.5,80,330/- and the insurance company approved a sum of Rs.4,00,000/- and further added Rs.40,000/- towards 10% dep, then it comes to Rs.2,20,330/- and in that amount a sum of Rs.1,10,000/- paid as advance and a sum of Rs.1,10,330/- is due.

sentences.text: Further the petitioner has calculated the medical bills in page number wise.
Further some of the bills produced they are advance receipts, hence they are not considered.

Hence the petitioner is entitled for Rs.10,62,756/- - Rs.4,00,000/- = Rs.6,62,756/-
which is rounded off to Rs.6,62,800/- towards medical expenses.
24. LOSS OF FUTURE INCOME DUE TO DISABILITY:
As per Sarla Verma's case, the appropriate multiplier applicable is '18'.
This Tribunal has already assessed the notional income of the petitioner at Rs.20,000/- p.m.
Hence a sum of Rs.12,09,600/- (Rs.20,000 X 12 X 18 X 28/100) is awarded under this head.
25. LOSS OF FUTURE AMENITIES AND HAPPINESS:
The disability referred above would have necessarily caused physical deformity with which the petitioner has to live the rest of his life.
Hence a sum of Rs.60,000/- is awarded under this head.

26. LOSS OF FUTURE & MATRIMONIAL PROSPECTS:
The accident & resultant disability would definitely hamper the petitioner's prospect of getting any suitable employment in future.
Someway or the other the disability would affect his future prospects both professionally and personally.
Obviously the matrimonial prospects of the victim/ petitioner who suffered grievous accidental injuries at the age of 20 years, would severely be affected.
For the loss that the petitioner shall suffer in this regard ends of justice would be met if he is awarded a compensation of Rs.80,000/- under this head.

REGARDING INTEREST & LIABILITY:
Having regard to the nature of the claim and current bank rate of interest, this Tribunal is of the view that if interest at the rate of 6% per annum is awarded it would meet the ends of justice.
30. It is contended in para 3 of the written statement that respondent. No.2 has not issued any policy.

It is pertinent to note that IO has given Notice u/s 133 of IMV Act as per Ex.P.4 and the said notice was replied as per Ex.P.9 wherein the owner of the offending car has admitted the involvement of the vehicle and in the reply he has clearly mentioned the car number as KA-51-AA-7363 and the issuance of insurance company name as IFFCO Tokio Gen.Ins.Co.Ltd., vide policy No.TIT/92386622 and same is valid till 16.02.2025.
Further the accident is occurred on 30.03.2024.

However careful perusal of policy which is found in documents as per the contents of which the issuance of insurance policy is respect of car bearing Reg.No.KA-51-AA-7363 covering the date of accident.
Hence, there is no dispute with regard to the issuance of insurance policy and its validity as on the date of accident.

Therefore, the respondent No.1 being the owner of the car bearing Reg.No.KA-51-AA-7363 and respondent No.2 being the insurer thereof are jointly and severally liable to pay the aforesaid award amount to the petitioner together with interest @ 6% per annum from the date of claim petition till realization of the entire amount.
However the respondent No.2 being the insurer is primarily liable to satisfy the award amount together with interest within one month from the date of this order.

Hence this issue is answered as 'Partly in the Affirmative'.
31. ISSUE NO.3 :

In view of the discussion made supra, this Tribunal proceeds to pass the following :
ORDER

The petition filed under Section 166 of M.V. Act 1988, is hereby partly allowed with costs in the following terms :
The petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.23,82,900/- with interest at the rate of 6% p.a., from the date of claim petition till realization of the entire award amount.

opennyai_summary.facts:
This claim petition is filed under section 166 of the M.V. Act, seeking compensation for the injuries sustained in a road traffic accident.
The respondent No.1 & 2 being the owner and insurer are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation, as such prayed to grant a compensation amount.
3. Notice was duly served to respondent No.1, the respondent No.1 did not appear before this Tribunal.
4. After service of notice, respondent No.2 filed written statement by contending that the petition itself is not maintainable either law or on facts.
opennyai_summary.issue:
Whether the petitioner proves that he sustained injuries in a road traffic accident that occurred on 30.03.2024 at about 2.30 a.m., near Sanjeeviningar cross, on B.B.
Road, Kodegehalli Flyover towards Airport, Bengaluru City due to actionable negligence of the driver of car bearing Reg.No.KA-51-AA-7363 ?
2) Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation as prayed for ? If so, at what rate and from whom ?
3) What order or award ?
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
In this view of the matter, no negligence can be imputed on the part of the petitioner and it is amply clear that the resultant accident occurred due to the sole negligence of the driver of car bearing Reg.No.KA-51-AA-7363.
Hence the Mohammed Ashique R Allias Muhammed ... vs Roopa Murthy on 2 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/69234192/
3
There is nothing on record to believe that the charge sheet filed by the police is defective or collusive.
In the present case nothing is placed on record to show that there was sufficient reason for the driver of the car to apply sudden brakes.
Even otherwise when the charge sheet is filed against the driver of the car for rash and negligent driving, burden was cast on the owner as well as insurer thereof to disprove the same.
Claimants cannot be called upon to prove a negative factor.
For the best reasons known to him, the owner of the offending car (respondent No.1) failed to appear before this Tribunal despite due service of the notice of petition upon him.
Accordingly an adverse inference could be drawn against him that he has impliedly admitted the petition averments.
10. Though the respondent No.2 Insurance company denied the cause of the accident, it has not let in any cogent evidence to prove its defence.
No independent witness was either produced by the insurer of the car to displace the version of the accident as deposed by PW.1 in this case.
Hence the respondents No.2 utterly failed to discharge the burden that was placed on them.
There is no explanation to that effect.
Non-examination of the said driver is fatal to the defence of respondent No.2.
Further in the decision of Hon'ble Apex Court in (2015) 2 SCC 180 (Ashwinbhai Jayantilal Modi vs.
Ramkaran Ramachandra Sharma and another) wherein for a MBBS student, the Court has taken the income as Rs.25,000/- p.m.
It is relevant to note that the deceased was pursuing B.P.T, degree.
The Bachelor of Physiotherepy cannot be equated with the B.E. or MBBS.
But the mere fact of petitioner pursuing his BPT Course goes to show that he had bright future.
The loss of earning capacity is something that will have to be assessed by the Tribunal with reference to the evidence in entirety.
Accordingly the compensation for the loss of the petitioner's future earning must be computed on that basis.
However careful perusal of policy which is found in documents as per the contents of which the issuance of insurance policy is respect of car bearing Reg.No.KA-51-AA-7363 covering the date of accident.
Hence, there is no dispute with regard to the issuance of insurance policy and its validity as on the date of accident.
Therefore, the respondent No.1 being the owner of the car bearing Reg.No.KA-51-AA-7363 and respondent No.2 being the insurer thereof are jointly and severally liable to pay the aforesaid award amount to the petitioner together with interest @ 6% per annum from the date of claim petition till realization of the entire amount.

opennyai_summary.decision:
Hence this issue is answered as 'Partly in the Affirmative'.
31. ISSUE NO.3 :
In view of the discussion made supra, this Tribunal proceeds to pass the following :
ORDER
The petition filed under Section 166 of M.V. Act 1988, is hereby partly allowed with costs in the following terms :
The petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.23,82,900/- with interest at the rate of 6% p.a., from the date of claim petition till realization of the entire award amount.
Mohammed
The respondent No.2 is liable to pay and directed to deposit the compensation amount within a period of one month from the date of award.
Out of the above said compensation amount awarded to the petitioner, 80% of the award amount with accrued interest shall be paid to him through NEFT/RTGS by way of E-payment on proper identification and due verification and further 20% of the award amount shall be kept in FD in favour of petitioner in any Nationalized or Scheduled bank for a period of 3 years.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.
